Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you put together a prompt for an update about the museum audio guide changes? the guide is for the north gallery, and the team replaced six two-minute recordings with clips that run about 75 seconds. the new clips use first-person accounts from three local residents, and the old version used curator narration. the launch was on april 12. visitors can still choose english or spanish, and the spanish recordings have not been revised yet. please ask for an update that explains what changed and gives the team a way to compare the old and new versions using the feedback cards collected at the desk. there were 48 cards between april 12 and may 3, but 11 of them had no comment about the guide, so don't treat all 48 as useful comments. staff also logged that the audio player in room 2 was unavailable for two afternoons because its charging cable was missing; it was back in use on april 25. don't claim this was the only reason for negative feedback, since the cards don't ask why someone disliked a clip. keep the update focused on these changes and the available feedback, not other museum services. it needs a final section called “Latest assessment” and that section should include the complete last assessment: “On the six-week gallery pilot, visitor feedback suggests the shorter clips are easier to follow; this does not establish that visitors learned more, and it covers only the three rooms tested.”", "output": "Write an update for the museum team about changes to the north gallery audio guide and the feedback available so far. Keep the update focused on these changes and the available feedback, rather than other museum services.

Include these details:
- The guide launched on April 12. Six two-minute recordings were replaced with clips of about 75 seconds.
- The new clips use first-person accounts from three local residents; the previous version used curator narration.
- Visitors can still choose English or Spanish. The Spanish recordings have not yet been revised.
- There were 48 feedback cards collected at the desk between April 12 and May 3. Eleven had no comment about the guide, so distinguish those from cards with useful comments. Explain how the team could compare the old and new versions using the available feedback.
- The audio player in room 2 was unavailable for two afternoons because its charging cable was missing and was back in use on April 25. Do not claim this was the only reason for negative feedback: the cards do not ask why someone disliked a clip.

End with a section titled “Latest assessment” and include the complete last assessment: “On the six-week gallery pilot, visitor feedback suggests the shorter clips are easier to follow; this does not establish that visitors learned more, and it covers only the three rooms tested.”"}]
